summary: AstroBalance: Interplanetary Survival Academy is an interactive, browser-based educational game for kids ages 7–12 that turns complex space mission engineering into hands-on play. Guided through a 5-stage narrative journey—from selecting a lunar or Martian outpost to surviving endless space hazards—students manage competing demands across three core systems: Power, Life Support, and Radiation Shielding. Grounded in real NASA and CSA datasets, every choice carries a genuine trade-off, teaching young learners how astronauts survive deep space.
details:
What does it do & how does it work?
AstroBalance is a 5-stage interactive web application designed to teach students ages 7–12 the real engineering trade-offs of running a lunar (Artemis Base Camp) or Martian (Outpost Alpha) habitat:
  • Stage 1 (Destination Hub): Players compare real environmental telemetry—gravity, day/night cycles (14-day lunar night vs. Martian Sols), temperature extremes, and communication delays (1.3s vs. 4–24 min)—before locking in their site.
  • Stage 2 (Pre-Flight Academy): Features a kid-friendly survival guide, a live space jargon decoder (translating terms like Regolith, ECLSS, and Sol in plain language), and historical mission lessons like the Apollo 13 CO2 filter crisis.
  • Stage 3 (Flight Certification): Includes an interactive Payload Mass vs. Radiation Shielding calculator (5,000 kg cargo cap) and a readiness quiz that unlocks the command console.
  • Stage 4 (Endless Outpost Simulator): Players manage three core gauges—Power Grid, Life Support (Air & Food), and Radiation Shielding—against randomized space weather and crew health crises where no choice is free.
  • Stage 5 (Global Leaderboard & Badge): Generates a verifiable Junior Commander certificate and logs survival scores on an interactive global leaderboard.
Impact, Creativity & Tools Used
By limiting gameplay to three visual gauges and explaining jargon in-context, AstroBalance bridges the gap between overly simplistic space posters and complex engineering spreadsheets. We developed the frontend and interactive simulation logic using React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Lovable, hosted open-source on GitHub.
